title: Where fossil-fuel CO2 came from in 1850
hook: Several countries burned coal by 1850. How was the world's fossil-fuel CO2 split?

doesNotKnow: how concentrated early fossil-fuel emissions were in one country
that a share can fall while the total rises

misconception: Early industrial emissions were spread across the industrial countries.
objective: The learner can say that in 1850 the United Kingdom produced about 62% of the world's fossil-fuel CO2, that its share fell to about 21% by 1900 while its own tonnes rose (122 to 420 Mt) and the world's grew about 10 times, and that a falling share can hide a rising total.

claims.text: Counting land cleared for farms too, the United Kingdom's 1850 share was under 5% (reveal, second clause of the limit sentence): co2_including_luc 1850, United Kingdom 131.8 Mt of a world 2,910.9 Mt = 4.5%.

'Land cleared for farms' describes land-use change: the research note (section 3) says 'mostly clearing forests and grasslands'; cm-history chose 'land cleared for farms too' over the reviewer's 'forests cleared for farms' (brief 9, change 3). Brief claims 2-3 (new).
claims.note: v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-16): NEW claim, unverified. Two parts for the fact-checker: the number (data, pinned file) and the gloss 'land cleared for farms' for land-use change (the note's 'mostly clearing forests and grasslands' does not itself say 'for farms'; I did not open a source that does). | FC pass 64 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16, SO-10-2 trigger d [project:history], server 6838dbac, R3a pass; walkthrough transcript 2026-10-16T14:28Z read first; own node script on the pinned owid-co2-data.csv, sha256 7f78e2b2... re-checked, and on Demo.tsx RAW: 1,005 values, 0 mismatches against the file rounded to 0.1 Mt): DISPUTED (blocks). The number re-derives: co2_including_luc 1850 UK 131.764, World 2,910.870 Mt = 4.527% (= co2 + land_use_change_co2 to 0.001 Mt; World LUC 2,714.022 is 93% of the denominator). Two problems. (1) 'Under 5%' states a bound sharper than the dataset supports. OWID's own caveat (ourworldindata.org/co2-dataset-sources, opened today): 'there is significant uncertainty in land use change emissions – significantly more than emissions from fossil fuels', and 'Since the estimates of emissions for fossil fuels and industry are much more certain than for land use change, we still adopt the former as our main CO2 emissions metric.' The central value is 0.47 points under the line; if world land-use CO2 in 1850 were about 10% lower, the share would be 5.0% (131.8/(0.9 x 2,714.0 + 196.8)). So 'roughly' is warranted. (2) 'For farms' has no opened source. The OWID files I opened describe land-use change as 'deforestation or reforestation' and 'land use change, deforestation, soils, or vegetation'; none says what the land was cleared for. The research note's 'mostly clearing forests and grasslands' has no source in the note and does not say 'for farms' either. FIX (builder; wording choice cm-history): 'counting land clearing too, the United Kingdom's 1850 share was roughly 5%' (or 'only a few percent'). Keep the claim text's number as 4.5%. cm-history should check that 'roughly 5%' in the reveal does not read as confirming the predict option 'About 5%' (that is a pedagogy call, not mine). If 'for farms' must stay, research-lead needs an opened source that says 1850 land-use CO2 was mostly clearing for agriculture (the GCB paper and globalcarbonbudget.org did not connect from this host today).

recall.question: One town makes 9 of 10 bicycles in a region. Fifty years later it makes twice as many, but the region makes ten times as many. Its share?
recall.why: 18 of 100 is 18%: the town's output doubled, but the total grew ten times, so its share fell to a fifth. A falling share can hide a rising total.
